title: An Ensemble of Fine-Tuned Convolutional Neural Networks for Medical Image Classification

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《An Ensemble of Fine-Tuned Convolutional Neural Networks for Medical Image Classification》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】The availability of medical imaging data from clinical archives, research literature, and clinical manuals, coupled with recent advances in computer vision offer the opportunity for image-based diagnosis, teaching, and biomedical research.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《An Ensemble of Fine-Tuned Convolutional Neural Networks for Medical Image Classification》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-4】This challenge is compounded by variations in the appearance of images based on the diseases depicted and a lack of sufficient training data for some modalities.

【Abstract · abstract-1-11】Our experiments on the ImageCLEF 2016 medical image public dataset (30 modalities; 6776 training images, and 4166 test images) show that our ensemble of fine-tuned CNNs achieves a higher accuracy than established CNNs.

Our experiments on the ImageCLEF 2016 medical image public dataset (30 modalities; 6776 training images, and 4166 test images) show that our ensemble of fine-tuned CNNs achieves a higher accuracy than established CNNs.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《An Ensemble of Fine-Tuned Convolutional Neural Networks for Medical Image Classification》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Abstract · abstract-1-11】Our experiments on the ImageCLEF 2016 medical image public dataset (30 modalities; 6776 training images, and 4166 test images) show that our ensemble of fine-tuned CNNs achieves a higher accuracy than established CNNs.

【Abstract · abstract-1-12】Our ensemble also achieves a higher accuracy than methods in the literature evaluated on the same benchmark dataset and is only overtaken by those methods that source additional training data.

evidence.text: Our experiments on the ImageCLEF 2016 medical image public dataset (30 modalities; 6776 training images, and 4166 test images) show that our ensemble of fine-tuned CNNs achieves a higher accuracy than established CNNs.
Our ensemble also achieves a higher accuracy than methods in the literature evaluated on the same benchmark dataset and is only overtaken by those methods that source additional training data.
